evidence.quote:
the frigidity of his
habitation\u2014some fifty-five or fifty-six degrees Fahrenheit\u2014was
maintained by an absorption system of ammonia cooling, the gasoline
engine whose pumps I had often heard in my room below.
evidence.paraphrase: The doctor's cold room is explained as being maintained by an ammonia absorption cooling system driven by a gasoline engine.

evidence.quote:
will and consciousness are
stronger than organic life itself, so that if a bodily frame be
but originally healthy and carefully preserved, it may through a
scientific enhancement of these qualities retain a kind of nervous
animation despite the most serious impairments, defects, or even
absences in the battery of specific organs.
evidence.paraphrase: The doctor theorizes that a carefully preserved body can retain nervous animation through enhanced will and consciousness even when organs fail.

evidence.quote:
He might, he half-jestingly
said, some day teach me to live\u2014or at least to possess some kind
of conscious existence\u2014without any heart at all!
evidence.paraphrase: The doctor suggests his theory could allow conscious existence without a functioning heart.

evidence.quote:
he had sunk his fortune and lost all his friends
in a lifetime of bizarre experiment devoted to its bafflement and
extirpation
evidence.paraphrase: The doctor is described as having spent his life on bizarre experiments aimed at defeating death.

evidence.quote:
he did not scorn
the incantations of the medi\u00e6valists, since he believed these cryptic
formul\u00e6 to contain rare psychological stimuli which might conceivably
have singular effects on the substance of a nervous system from which
organic pulsations had fled
evidence.paraphrase: The doctor treats medieval incantations as psychological stimuli that could affect a nervous system no longer driven by organic function.

evidence.quote:
with my aid he amplified the
ammonia piping of his room and modified the pumps and feed of his
refrigerating machine until he could keep the temperature as low as
thirty-four or forty degrees, and finally even twenty-eight degrees
evidence.paraphrase: The doctor progressively modifies his refrigeration machinery to achieve ever colder temperatures.

evidence.quote:
One night about eleven the pump of the
refrigerating machine broke down, so that within three hours the
process of ammonia cooling became impossible.
evidence.paraphrase: The refrigeration pump breaks down, ending the ammonia cooling that sustains the doctor.

evidence.quote:
Only his
lividly inclined complexion and coldness of touch could have afforded
a physical basis for this feeling, and even these things should have
been excusable considering the man's known invalidism.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator feels a repugnance he cannot justify beyond the doctor's livid complexion and cold touch.

evidence.quote:
all
that I can say is that I hate the smell of ammonia, and grow faint at a
draft of unusually cool air.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator's lasting reaction is a hatred of ammonia smell and faintness at cool air.

evidence.quote:
It had to be done my way\u2014artificial preservation\u2014 for you
see I died that time eighteen years ago .
evidence.paraphrase: The final note reveals the doctor actually died eighteen years earlier and had been artificially preserved.

evidence.quote:
Warmer every minute, and the tissues can't last.
I fancy you know\u2014what I said about the will and the nerves and the
preserved body after the organs ceased to work. It was good theory, but
couldn't keep up indefinitely. There was a gradual deterioration I had
not foreseen.
evidence.paraphrase: The note explains that the preservation theory failed because warming tissues deteriorate and the method could not be sustained.

evidence.quote:
One September day an
unexpected glimpse of him induced an epileptic fit in a man who had
come to repair his electric desk lamp; a fit for which he prescribed
effectively while keeping himself well out of sight.
evidence.paraphrase: A repairman is thrown into an epileptic fit by an unexpected glimpse of the doctor.

evidence.quote:
It is a mistake to fancy that horror is associated inextricably
with darkness, silence, and solitude. I found it in the glare of
midafternoon, in the clangor of a metropolis
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts expected associations of horror with the ordinary daylit urban setting where he encountered it.
